mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly reduces the discount rate applied to equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as a continuous trend without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.2% is associated with negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate above 9.0% indicates a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE > 9.0%, or the rank IC between UNRATE and 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high unemployment (UNRATE > 9.0%) and weak job growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.1% month-over-month) indicates a deteriorating labor market that reduces consumer confidence and corporate investment, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of UNRATE > 9.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.1% occurs in more than 60% of cases where SPX 20-day returns are positive, or the rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, elevated housing starts (HOUST > 600,000 units) signal overvaluation in the real estate sector and potential economic overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods when HOUST > 600,000, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the rank IC between HOUST and 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production below 95 (index 2017=100) indicates a contraction in the manufacturing sector, reducing corporate earnings and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 95, or the rank IC between INDPRO and 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) supports sustained monetary easing that boosts equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as a continuous trend without threshold conditions.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS below 0.2% is associated with negative 60-day returns in more than 60% of cases, or the rank IC between FEDFUNDS and 60-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak retail sales growth (RSAFS growth < 0.2% month-over-month) and high inflation (CPIAUCSL growth > 2.5% year-over-year) indicates stagflationary pressures that reduce consumer purchasing power and corporate margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition of RSAFS growth < 0.2% and CPIAUCSL growth > 2.5% occurs in more than 60% of cases where SPX 20-day returns are positive, or the rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index above 220 (CPIAUCSL > 220) signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 220, or the rank IC between CPIAUCSL and 5-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
